sources.claim: The Ethereum Foundation Soldogn recap says the week ended with a stable multi-client Glamsterdam devnet running the latest ePBS, repricing, and block access list specs, and that nearly all clients were running together on glamsterdam-devnet-2 with the external builders pipeline tested end-to-end.
sources.notes: This source supports devnet/interoperability context, not production release compatibility.

sources.claim: The EthPandaOps glamsterdam-devnet-2 spec lists a Kurtosis participants matrix with geth as the execution client image and prysm, lodestar, lighthouse, teku, nimbus, and grandine as consensus client images.
sources.notes: This source supports devnet participant examples. It does not claim mainnet-ready client releases.

sources.claim: The consensus-specs v1.7.0-alpha.7 release is a pre-release containing Gloas changes used by the glamsterdam-devnet-2 spec.
sources.notes: Spec release metadata is useful provenance for devnet test entries, but is not a client release.

sources.claim: The execution-spec-tests bal@v5.6.1 pre-release is labeled for bal-devnet-3 v7 and includes BAL/state-gas test updates referenced by the glamsterdam-devnet-2 spec.
sources.notes: Spec-test release metadata is useful provenance for devnet test entries, but is not a client release.

sources.claim: Geth v1.17.3 release notes describe continued progress on the Amsterdam fork implementation, including prerequisites for EIP-7928, EIP-8037, EIP-7976, EIP-7981, EIP-7610, and updated state tests.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Nethermind v1.37.2 release notes describe healthcheck and archive invalid-block fixes for v1.37.1 and do not state Glamsterdam or Amsterdam readiness.
sources.notes: Latest release reviewed. No explicit Glamsterdam/Amsterdam readiness signal found in this release note.

sources.claim: Besu 26.5.0 release notes include Block Access List pipeline work, EIP-7928 Block Access List budget enforcement, Block Access List index encoding changes, and adding EIP-7981 to Amsterdam.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Reth v2.2.0 release notes say the release lays groundwork for Amsterdam EIP-7928 Block Access Lists, with BAL store, P2P wire support, payload-builder integration, and parallel/batched BAL execution paths.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. The notes call this groundwork and mention gated paths, not complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Lighthouse v8.1.3 release notes describe maintenance fixes and do not state Glamsterdam, Amsterdam, or Gloas readiness.
sources.notes: Latest release reviewed. Use the v8.1.0 row for the explicit Gloas release-note signal.

sources.claim: Lighthouse v8.1.0 release notes include Gloas gossip boilerplate, Gloas data column support, consensus types updated for Gloas v1.7.0-alpha.1, Gloas off-protocol payment fields, and EIP-7732 Gloas containers/constants.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Lodestar v1.42.0 release notes say the release makes great strides toward the Gloas hard fork and list Gloas network processor, data-column sidecar, payload-envelope pipeline, voluntary-exit, and ePBS state-cache work.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Prysm v7.1.3 release notes describe extensive Gloas groundwork and list Gloas builder support, latest execution bid processing, proposer slashing, beacon API block returns, payload attestation processing, and Gloas timing intervals.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Teku 26.4.0 release notes include the PostPtcDuties REST API endpoint for the Gloas API.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.

sources.claim: Nimbus v26.3.1 release notes describe Ethereum column-handling performance, validator robustness, Gnosis Fulu scheduling, and fast-confirmation work, but do not state Glamsterdam, Amsterdam, or Gloas readiness.
sources.notes: Latest release reviewed. No explicit Glamsterdam/Amsterdam/Gloas readiness signal found in this release note.

sources.claim: Grandine 2.0.4 release notes include post-Gloas beacon block API publishing, execution payload bid endpoints, payload attestation ticks, and consensus spec tests v1.7.0-alpha.3.
sources.notes: Client release-note provenance only. This does not assert complete Glamsterdam production compatibility.
